minutes.headline: Committee agreed to launch the revised Plan Lunenburg survey without a vote, with edits and an email opt-in to be added.
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee reviewed the revised eight-goal community survey with the consultants, suggesting edits such as links, clearer example strategies, fact checks and an optional contact opt-in. Members agreed the survey could launch without a formal vote, then discussed the May 30 public workshop, a possible Sunday session, committee membership and email list problems, the lack of a clerk and unapproved minutes, and the chair's limited availability. The meeting adjourned by roll call.

A member said the schools face layoffs and programmatic cuts if funding is not addressed.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed the revised Plan Lunenburg survey could launch without a formal vote, once edits and an optional email opt-in are added.
Members reviewed the eight-goal survey with the consultants and asked for edits to links, example strategies and fact checks.
Members said the posted 2024 minutes were never approved and that the roster does not match the website or the email list; the chair is to ask the town website staff to fix the list.
The committee is to ask about an extra Sunday session beyond the May 30 public workshop, and meetings are to return to the first Thursday of the month.
The next agenda is to cover a clerk volunteer, review of the minutes, a May 30 update, swearing-in status and absent members.

why_it_matters: The survey is the main way residents can say what Lunenburg's master plan should prioritize, including housing, farmland, school facilities and a possible stormwater fund charged to property owners.
The minutes problems and the email list mismatch affect whether residents can find out about meetings and the workshop, and whether the committee's record can be relied on.
watch_next: The May 30 public workshop on the master plan.
The next committee agenda: clerk volunteer, review of the posted minutes, and the survey launch.
